title: Two-sided inverse to degreewise currying
statement: For every site C with topology J, sheaf R of commutative rings in universe max u v, cochain complexes K,L,M of R-modules, and integer n, there exists one reverse morphism b from homComplex (Tot(K tensor L)) M in degree n to homComplex K (homComplex L M) in degree n such that, for every forward morphism a satisfying the localized pure-tensor currying equation of lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise (expanded verbatim in the Lean statement), a followed by b and b followed by a are identity morphisms. No existence of a forward map is asserted; b is constructed independently of a.

proof.text: Obtain b and its localized evaluation equality from homTensorDegreewise_reverse_construct. This construction is independent of a. Fix any forward morphism a satisfying HomTensorDegreewiseEquation; keep this b for both composites.

For a followed by b, use the Hom-complex product cone from homComplex_projections_exists to compare the p projections. Apply extensionality of localized presheaf-module morphisms and inner Hom-complex sections. The naturality formula for an inner Hom section moves its evaluation over V -> W to evaluation over the identity of V, with the input section restricted to V. Naturality of the outer localized morphism similarly moves x to K^p(V). At the composite V -> U, the reverse equation for a(s) and forward equation for s have identical tensor evaluations, so their iterated Hom evaluations agree. Product and module-morphism extensionality give a followed by b equal to the identity. The private restriction-evaluation and product-extensionality helpers are proved directly in Lean.

For b followed by a, compare the total-degree Hom projections by product extensionality. The private localized tensor extensionality helper transposes a morphism X -> Hom(T,N) to T -> Hom(X,N) by the concrete presheaf tensor-Hom equivalence with coefficient and module universe max u v w and symmetry; this transpose is injective. Restrict to each coproduct summand, cancel the tensor sheafification comparison and apply the sheafification adjunction, then compare sectionwise pure tensors. The forward equation on b(s) followed by the reverse equation on s gives equality on each such tensor. This proves the second composite identity and finishes the conjunction. No differential or boundedness result is used.

lean.statement:
theorem homTensorDegreewise_inverse (K L M : CochainComplex Mod ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R
    ∃ b : (homComplex (R := R)
        (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod)) M).X n ⟶
      (homComplex (R := R) K (homComplex (R := R) L M)).X n,
      ∀ a, HomTensorDegreewiseEquation R K L M n a → a ≫ b = 𝟙 _ ∧ b ≫ a = 𝟙 _
